verdict.rationale: Hatchet documents per-key concurrency limits set with CEL expressions (e.g. premium-tier users get 10 concurrent runs, others get 1). It also supports shared concurrency rules across workflows and per-key queue-depth strategies, so runs are not held in a single FIFO queue and each tenant or user key can be capped. However, nothing in the evidence shows assigning priorities to individual runs or an explicit fair-scheduling algorithm (such as round-robin across tenants). Missing for 10: explicit run-priority assignment, documented fair or round-robin scheduling across tenants, independent or hands-on corroboration.
